# Quark phase-2 web collection

Recorded on 2026-10-09 for flighthouse #28 with the production web runner
(`flighthouse collect` and the `web:` section of [`collect.yaml`](collect.yaml)).
Every change stayed in a disposable local checkout and backend; nothing was
pushed to quark and no quark source file was edited.

## Versions

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| quark source | `d8d2618ecb2c658f04f90f20c8a73e5fd987cbd1` (`main`, 2026-10-09) |
| quark backend | built from the same commit, `go build ./cmd/quark`, go1.27.2 toolchain |
| Flutter / Dart | 3.47.7 / 3.13.5 |
| Browser | Chrome 152.0.7977.42, acquired by Dart Puppeteer 3.26.0 |
| Lighthouse | 13.5.0, run as `npx --yes lighthouse@13.5.0` on Node 26.8.2 |
| axe-core | 4.11.1, `axe.min.js` sha256 `7dbfabdfc6062936d79c873ddbb5f811a1219fca3928bd8cc9dd81f1e65f4720` |
| Dataset generator | ImageMagick 7.1.2-31 |

Startup semantics needed no opt-in change: quark
[#2919](https://github.com/autobutler-org/quark/pull/2919) already calls
`SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()` on the web, so the build is quark's
own `make build/frontend/web FLUTTER_BUILD_MODE=release`.

## Backend

The backend binary was built from the source commit and started with an
isolated home directory, so its database and files live under that directory
only:

```sh
mkdir -p internal/server/public && touch internal/server/public/stub.txt
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/autobutler-org/quark/pkg/util/versionutil.GitCommit=d8d2618e" \
  -o quark-server ./cmd/quark
HOME="$PWD/audit-home" PORT=18431 QUARK_INSECURE=true ./quark-server serve
```

`GET /api/v0/auth/status` answered `{"setup":false}` before provisioning. The
owner `audit-owner` was then created through quark's real `/setup` form in a
Puppeteer-driven browser. Quark derives the auth key in the client, so the API
cannot create the account directly. The password was generated locally and
never printed or committed.

## Collection

[`collect.yaml`](collect.yaml) is the exact config. Its `projectDir` expects the
quark checkout beside the flighthouse checkout (`../quark`). From flighthouse:

```sh
export FLIGHTHOUSE_QUARK_NAME=Audit
export FLIGHTHOUSE_QUARK_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:18431
export FLIGHTHOUSE_USERNAME=audit-owner
export FLIGHTHOUSE_PASSWORD=<generated>
make run/quark/web
```

`collect` built the app, served `build/web` on an OS-chosen loopback port,
launched the pinned Chrome at 1280×800 with device scale factor 1, signed in, and
ran Lighthouse (`--form-factor=desktop`, matching screen emulation, storage reset
disabled) and then axe (`ancestry: true`) on each route. It printed:

```text
browser Chrome/152.0.7977.42
collected 3 lighthouse files
collected 3 axe files
```

The recorded run used this branch plus the queued one-line focus fix from the
web-workflow branch (`focus: page.click` in `puppeteer_browser.dart`). A second
collection about ten minutes later, on this branch without that fix, also
signed in and collected all six files. Gated against this baseline, it showed
identical axe findings and accessibility and best-practices scores, but `/photos`
Lighthouse LCP went from 1.1 s to 8.1 s. Performance dropped from 58 to 50, and
the gate failed on one new serious `largest-contentful-paint` finding and the
score drops. `image-delivery-insight` on `/files` also changed fingerprint,
because Lighthouse named the splash image in one run and no node in the other.
The second run's outputs were not committed.

### Sign-in

Quark's web build assumes it is served by its own backend (default host `/`).
The runner's static server does not proxy `/api`, so the auth steps use quark's
own UI to add the backend as an absolute host. The backend allows cross-origin
bearer requests. The steps start at `/terms`, since a fresh browser has accepted
no terms:

1. Accept the terms for the default host.
2. On `/login`, open **Change**, then **Add Quark**, type the nickname and
   address, and **Save**. Quark switches to the new host and shows its terms.
3. Accept those terms, type the username and password into the real form, and
   activate **Sign in**. Wait for the Files filter chip `My files`.

Quark's buttons expose their names as text content, not `aria-label`, and the
add-host fields are labeled only by hint text that disappears once they hold a
value. The selectors are therefore structural (sibling and `:has()`
relationships between Flutter semantics nodes). They are specific to this
build and are the most fragile part of the recipe.

## Raw outputs

Files are named by the sha256 of the route. Every Lighthouse result has no
`runtimeError`, and its `finalDisplayedUrl` equals the requested route. The axe
results report the same URLs and a 1280-pixel window.

They live under
[`lighthouse/13.5.0/quark-d8d2618e`](../../lighthouse/13.5.0/quark-d8d2618e) and

contain no credential, session token, or recovery phrase; this was checked by
searching for each value.

## Replaying flighthouse

[`flighthouse.yaml`](flighthouse.yaml) imports the raw directories, so replay
needs no Node, Chrome, Flutter, or backend:

```sh
make test/quark/web
```

The committed [baseline](flighthouse-baseline.json) holds the 157 findings of
this run. `make test/cli` includes this gate.
